# Route Trace

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

An online traceroute (MTR) with a map. It runs from a [Globalping](https://globalping.io) probe that looks like your
own network, or from one next to the target for the way back to you, and shows every hop: the networks and lines it
crosses, where it leaves the country, which stretch takes a detour and where packets are really lost.

## How it works

Every request goes from your browser straight to public services; nothing passes through a server of this site.

| Step | Source |
|---|---|
| Your networks (home line and proxy exits) | the checks the 1ms.dog home page uses: `/_ms/me`, ipip.net, Cloudflare, ip.sb, ipinfo, IPv4-only and IPv6-only hosts, STUN; grouped by AS, data-centre networks marked as proxies |
| The probe | Globalping's probe list. Outbound: same AS, else the same carrier (mainland carriers by family), else nearby. Return: closest to where the outbound trace ended |
| The trace | Globalping MTR, one probe, 5–16 packets per hop |
| Where each hop is | PeeringDB (exchange points), router names (IATA and CLLI codes), GeoJS, then ipinfo for country-only answers |
| Who owns an unannounced address | RDAP |

`src/lib.mjs` turns the hops into a path:

- **Latency** at a hop is the lowest round trip of that hop and every later one: routers answer probes late, and a
  packet to a later hop passed this one.
- **Loss** counts only when it lasts to the end of the path; a hop that drops answers while later hops are fine is
  only busy.
- **The probe's own LAN** (private and CGNAT hops before the first public one) is left out.
- **Places** must fit the latency: light in fibre covers about 100 km per millisecond of round trip, so a place
  farther from the probe than the round trip allows is dropped, and so is a guessed place the hops around it rule out.
  A geo database's city for an address nobody announces in BGP is only where the block is registered, so it's shown
  with a question mark.
- **Jumps**: the biggest rise in latency is explained by the fibre round trip to a far place seen later on the path,
  or by the country the path enters.
- **Lines** are named: China Telecom CN2, 163 and CTG; China Unicom 169, 9929 and CUG; China Mobile CMNET, CMI and
  CMIN2; exchange points; the big transit and cloud networks.

A trace can be shared as a link, `/<lang>/r/<code>`, that holds the hops and their places (`src/code.mjs`), so it
opens the same after Globalping's result has expired. On a return trace the target is your own IP: the link and the
card keep only its first half unless you tick the box in the share dialog.

## Develop

```bash
npm install
npm run build      # public/ from src/ (pages in 10 languages, hashed assets)
npm test           # build check, unit tests, i18n coverage
npm run dev        # wrangler dev on :8807
npm run assets     # og images (resvg)
```

Strings live in `src/i18n/<lang>.mjs`; `zh-CN` is the reference and every language must have the same keys and
placeholders (`test/i18n.test.mjs`). City names per language are in `src/cities.mjs`.
